approachQuestion.prompt:
Check the Striped Grid

A rectangular integer grid is striped when every diagonal running from top-left toward bottom-right has a single constant value. Return whether grid is striped. Different diagonals may have different values.

Example 1: grid=[[4,7,2],[8,4,7]] → true.
Example 2: grid=[[4,7],[8,5]] → false.
Example 3: grid=[[3,1,9]] → true.

Constraints:
1 ≤ r,c ≤ 200,000; r*c ≤ 200,000. Every row has exactly c values.
Values are integers between −10^9 and 10^9. Do not modify grid.
A one-row or one-column grid is striped. Return one Boolean.
constraints: 1 ≤ r,c ≤ 200,000; r*c ≤ 200,000. Every row has exactly c values.
Values are integers between −10^9 and 10^9. Do not modify grid.
A one-row or one-column grid is striped. Return one Boolean.

options.text: For each cell with both row and column greater than zero, compare it with the cell one row up and one column left. Reject on a mismatch; otherwise accept.
options.feedback: Consecutive equalities link all members of each required diagonal. Border cells have no predecessor and impose no extra relation.

options.text: Copy values from every top-left-to-bottom-right diagonal into separate temporary lists. Verify each list has a single value.
options.feedback: The copied lists test exactly the right groups, but storing them is unnecessary: each cell can be compared to its direct diagonal predecessor.

options.text: Compare each cell that has one with its upper-right neighbor. Accept if all those comparisons match.
options.feedback: That checks the opposite diagonal direction. [[1,2],[2,3]] passes those comparisons, but its top-left-to-bottom-right diagonal contains 1 and 3.

options.text: Accept only when every grid cell equals grid[0][0].
options.feedback: Different diagonals may differ. [[1,2],[3,1]] is striped, but this method rejects it.

feedback.reason: Matching every cell to its upper-left neighbor propagates equality along each diagonal.
details: Visit rows after the first and columns after the first. Compare each such cell with its upper-left neighbor. Return false at a mismatch and true after all comparisons.

Matching every cell to its upper-left neighbor propagates equality along each diagonal. No comparison exists in a one-row matrix. A one-column matrix still incurs outer-loop overhead in this fixed implementation, so the precise degenerate-dimension cost follows its loops rather than a generic area slogan.

“For each cell with both row and column greater than zero, compare it with the cell one row up and one column left. Reject on a mismatch; otherwise accept.”: Consecutive equalities link all members of each required diagonal. Border cells have no predecessor and impose no extra relation.

“Copy values from every top-left-to-bottom-right diagonal into separate temporary lists. Verify each list has a single value.”: The copied lists test exactly the right groups, but storing them is unnecessary: each cell can be compared to its direct diagonal predecessor.

“Compare each cell that has one with its upper-right neighbor. Accept if all those comparisons match.”: That checks the opposite diagonal direction. [[1,2],[2,3]] passes those comparisons, but its top-left-to-bottom-right diagonal contains 1 and 3.
“Accept only when every grid cell equals grid[0][0].”: Different diagonals may differ. [[1,2],[3,1]] is striped, but this method rejects it.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method “Compare Diagonal Neighbors”, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let r and c denote the dimensions. Analyze the stated loops, including row-loop overhead when c=1. Use a tight bound valid for r=1 or c=1: the inner column loop has c−1 iterations and the outer loop has r−1. Indexed reads and comparisons cost constant time. Exclude input and Boolean output; include loop variables and stack. No copies, recursion or hashing.
constraints: 1 ≤ r,c ≤ 200,000; r*c ≤ 200,000. Every row has exactly c values.
Values are integers between −10^9 and 10^9. Do not modify grid.
A one-row or one-column grid is striped. Return one Boolean.

options.text: O(r*c) time and O(r*c) auxiliary space for all dimensions.
O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space for all dimensions.

feedback.reason: Count eligible diagonal comparisons and the fixed method's outer-loop overhead.
details: There are r−1 outer iterations, each with constant overhead and up to c−1 comparisons. Hence the tight worst-case bound for these precise loops is O(1+(r−1)*c). When r=1 they perform no row iterations; when c=1 they still iterate over the remaining rows. Only loop state is stored.
The option “O(1 + (r−1)*c) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: This includes empty-inner-loop overhead without requiring a scan for a single row.
The option “O(r*c) time and O(r*c) auxiliary space for all dimensions.”: The fixed method builds no copied grid or diagonal lists.
The option “O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space for all dimensions.”: With both dimensions large, all diagonal-neighbor comparisons may be needed.
The option “O((r*c)²) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: Each eligible pair is compared once.
